significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that adopting a false-believing persona causes a shift in the model's separately decoded own-belief state, that "the degree of own-belief contamination is measurable and predicts factual errors after role-play," and that steering a "belief-ownership" direction reduces those errors while preserving role-play. This is a form-(iii) predictive coupling between an internal contamination measure and later behavior, combined with a form-(ii) causal intervention; it establishes both a consequential phenomenon and a partial mechanism, fixing expectations about which role-play episodes will produce subsequent leakage rather than merely showing that beliefs are decodable, as in the latent-knowledge probing line represented by Burns et al.'s Discovering Latent Knowledge in Language Models Without Supervision. The claim is determinate, and a negative result—particularly no persona-specific shift beyond matched false-content controls and no prediction of later errors—would rule out this contamination account, although it would not rule out other sources of persona carryover. Topic-substitution check: replacing these specifics with the generic topic statement that LLMs represent item states would not justify this score; the predictive contamination-to-error relation and causal insulation are the above-median contribution.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "contamination score" as a diagnostic and predictor and the "belief-ownership" steering direction as an intervention. Because the score is asserted to "predict[] factual errors after role-play," it is ex ante with respect to the later own-voice error and can provide an action window for auditing or insulation, rather than merely explaining an error after it occurs. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction that greater contamination forecasts greater leakage should survive as a relation, but the hypothesis does not assert architecture-, scale-, or training-regime invariance, so its scope is best read as a class of persona-role-play tasks rather than an all-LLM law; likely downstream users include researchers and practitioners who audit or deploy persona-based systems. Topic-substitution check: generic research on LLM beliefs supplies neither this forward predictor nor the steering handle, so the reach score comes from the claim-specific handoff rather than the topic's general importance.
